chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him): A man bought a farm or a servant from a man with wealth that he had taken from banditry (cutting off the road) or from theft. Is it permissible for him to benefit from the fruits of this farm, or is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with this female servant whom he bought from the thief or from the bandit?
So he (peace be upon him) signed: There is no good in anything whose origin is prohibited, and it is not permissible to utilize it.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use property bought with stolen money?
ai.summary: Imam al-Hadi (AS) provides a comprehensive ruling by stating that 'no good' exists in anything whose origin is illicit, thereby prohibiting both the primary asset and its derived benefits, such as agricultural produce or marital relations with a purchased servant. This principle underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the impurity of the source (haram al-asl) contaminates the entire utility of the asset, extending beyond mere ownership to practical usage. The hadith highlights the holistic nature of purity in transaction, ensuring that gains from theft or banditry yield no legitimate benefit.
